content:
The test image shows a young soybean seedling with a dark brown, sunken lesion at/near the soil line on the hypocotyl/stem, with some grayish-white material around the affected area. This points toward a damping-off or seedling blight disease.

Top candidates:
- **Rhizoctonia**: reddish-brown, sunken, firm, dry lesions at the hypocotyl soil line
- **Pythium_damping_off**: water-soaked, soft brown rot on hypocotyl
- **Phytophthora**: dark brown lesion extending up from taproot

The Rhizoctonia reference shows reddish-brown, sunken lesions on seedling hypocotyls at the soil line — this matches the test image closely. The test image shows a young seedling with a dark brown, sunken, firm-looking lesion at the stem near the soil line, with grayish appearance (possibly mycelium/soil). The lesion character (sunken, dry, dark reddish-brown at the node) is a strong match for Rhizoctonia.
